◆ c_action_ac_implied_do()

void c_action_ac_implied_do ( )

Performs the implementation of the ac_implied_do action.

Processes and constructs an implicit DO expression for Fortran.

This function serves as the implementation layer for the ac_implied_do action. Currently, the implementation is a placeholder that logs the action name and the number of arguments to the standard output using printf.

Precondition
None.
Postcondition
The function prints a formatted string to the standard output.
Note
This function is currently a stub and does not process any actual arguments.

This function implements the logic for handling Fortran AC (Array Constructor) implied DO expressions. It retrieves loop control information (lower bound, upper bound, and increment) from the front of the astExpressionStack, extracts the elements from a SgExprListExp container, and constructs a new SgImpliedDo object. The function also handles the assembly of the object list (the elements being constructed) by popping the next available expression from the stack and appending it to a new SgExprListExp.

The implementation relies on a specific sequence of rule processing (R470 and R471) where loop control information is passed via the astExpressionStack.

Precondition
The astExpressionStack must not be empty.
The first element of astExpressionStack must be a valid SgExprListExp containing exactly three expressions (lower bound, upper bound, and increment).
The astExpressionStack must contain at least one additional expression representing the entry for the objectList.
Postcondition
The SgImpliedDo object is constructed and pushed to the front of astExpressionStack.
The SrgExprListExp containing loop control information is deleted.
The parent pointers of the loop control expressions (lower bound, upper bound, and increment) are updated to point to the new SgImpliedDo object.
Note
This function uses if blocks for debugging and state output via outputState.
The function assumes that the loop control information is provided by a previous rule (R471) and passed through the stack.

This function serves as an implementation of the ac_implied_do_control action. It performs a diagnostic trace by printing the function name, the number of arguments passed, and the specific value of the first boolean argument to the standard output.

Parameters
carg_0A boolean flag representing the first argument of the action.

This function implements the logic for handling implied DO loops by popping necessary components from the expression and name stacks. It retrieves the loop bounds (lower and upper) and an optional stride/increment value from the astExpressionStack. It also retrieves the loop variable name from the astNameStack. The function constructs an assignment expression to initialize the loop variable to the lower bound and then assembles a SgExprListExp containing the initialization, upper bound, and increment. This constructed list is then pushed back onto the astExpressionStack.

Parameters
hasStrideA boolean flag indicating whether a stride/increment expression is present on the astExpressionStack. If true, the function pops an additional expression to use as the increment.
Precondition
The astExpressionStack must contain at least two elements (lower bound and upper bound). If hasStride is true, the stack must contain at least three elements.
The astNameStack must not be empty, as it is used to retrieve the loop variable name.
The variable name retrieved from astNameStack must correspond to a valid SgVariableSymbol found within the current astScopeStack.
Postcondition
The astExpressionStack will have the lower bound, upper bound, and (optionally) the increment popped, and a new SgExprListExp pushed onto the front of the stack.
The astNameStack will have the loop variable name popped from the front.
Note
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the state of the stacks and the existence of the variable symbol.
If hasStride is false, a SgNullExpression is used as the increment.

This function takes a specified number of expressions from the front of the astExpressionStack and aggregates them into a single SgExprListExp object. The resulting expression list is then pushed back onto the front of the astExpressionStack. The function iterates through the count, popping elements from the stack and prepending them to the new list, effectively reversing or reordering the elements based on the prepend logic.

Parameters
countThe number of expressions to be pulled from the astExpressionStack and grouped into the new SgExprListExp.
Precondition
The astExpressionStack must not be empty if count is greater than or equal to 1.
Postcondition
If count >= 1, a new SgExprListExp is created and placed at the front of the astExpressionASSExpressionStack. If count < 1, the stack remains unchanged, but the function still asserts that the stack is not empty.
Note
This function uses new to allocate the SgExprListExp, so the caller or the AST management system is responsible for memory management.
The function includes debug logging that depends on the SgProject::get_verbose() level and the DEBUG_RULE_COMMENT_LEVEL macro.

This function is part of the semantic analysis process, specifically triggered during the processing of an AC value list. It checks if there is an expression on the astExpressionStack that is an SgExprListExp. If such an expression exists and the astAttributeSpecStack is not empty, the function attempts to convert the current type on the astTypeStack into an array type using convertTypeOnStackToArrayType. This is particularly relevant for handling Fortran-style array constructions where an expression defines the elements of the list.

The implementation involves popping the existing type from the astTypeStack and replacing it with the newly constructed array type, while also managing the astAttributeSpecStack by removing the dimension attribute specification.

Precondition
The astExpressionStack may contain an SgExprListExp.
The astAttributeSpecStack may contain dimension attributes (AttrSpec_DIMENSION or ComponentAttrSpec_dimension).
Postcondition
If a conversion occurs, the astTypeStack will contain the new SgArrayType instead of the previous base type.
If a conversion occurs, the top element of the astAttributeSpecStack is popped.
Note
This function relies on the global state of the AST stacks (astExpressionStack, astTypeStack, and astAttributeSpecStack).
Debugging information is printed to stdout if SgProject::get_verbose() exceeds DEBUG_RULE_COMMENT_LEVEL.
The function uses if and endif directives for conditional compilation of debugging and state output logic.

This function ensures that the astNodeStack is empty at the beginning of a new statement. This is necessary because certain processing steps, such as handling 'where' statements, may push predicate nodes onto the stack. If a 'where' statement is not encountered, these nodes remain on the stack, potentially corrupting subsequent statement processing. The function checks the current size of the stack and clears it if it is not empty.

Note
If SgProject::get_verbose() is set above the DEBUG_RULE_COMMENT_LEVEL, the current size of the stack is printed to the standard output.
If SgProject::get_verbose() is set above the DEBUG_COMMENT_LEVEL, a message indicating the clearing of the stack is printed to the standard output.
Precondition
The astNodeStack should be accessible within the current scope.
Postcondition
The astNodeStack is guaranteed to be empty after this function executes, regardless of its state prior to the call.

The function identifies the numerical base (binary, octal, or hexadecimal) based on the leading character of the token's text (e.g., 'B' for binary, 'O' for octal, 'Z' for hex) and then converts the remaining string content into a 64-bit integer. After conversion, a new SgLongLongIntVal expression is created, its source position is set to match the original token, and it is pushed onto the front of the astExpressionStack.

The source position of the new expression is synchronized with the input token.
Note
The function uses strtoll to perform the string-to-long-long conversion, starting the parsing from the third character of the token text (index 2).
This implementation treats boz constants as typeless until assignment.

It is responsible for creating a SgDerivedTypeStatement, associating it with the current scope, and managing the definition and declaration modifiers. It also handles the configuration of access modifiers to ensure consistency between defining and non-defining declarations.

This function enforces specific rules regarding internal stack handling during the construction phase of a C executable. It ensures that certain stacks, which should be empty once a statement has been fully processed, do not contain any leftover elements. Specifically, it checks that the astExpressionStack and astLabelSymbolStack are both empty. If the verbose logging level is set above DEBUG_RULE_COMMENT_LEVEL, the function prints the current sizes of the astExpressionStack and astNodeStack.

Warning
If the astExpressionStack or astLabelSymbolStack are found to be non-empty, an error message is printed to stdout and a ROSE_ASSERT failure is triggered.

The construction process for the current executable scope must have reached a point where all statements are completely processed.
Postcondition
The astExpressionStack and astLabelSymbolStack are guaranteed to be empty upon successful completion of the function.
Note

This function is used during the parsing process to handle type kind specifications, specifically for cases like "real*8" in C-style syntax. It evaluates the relationship between two tokens to determine if a numeric precision value should be extracted and pushed onto the astTypeKindStack, or if an existing expression should be transitioned into a type kind.

The implementation checks if token2 is not null and does not represent an assignment operator. If these conditions are met, it treats the text of token2 as an integer value, creates a new SgIntVal object, sets its source position, and pushes it onto the astTypeKindStack. Otherwise, it attempts to move the front element of the astExpressionStack to the astTypeKindStack.

Parameters
token1A pointer to the first token in the sequence.
token2A pointer to the second token in the sequence, used to identify numeric precision or assignment.
hasExpressionA boolean flag indicating whether an expression is present.
Precondition
The astExpressionStack must not be empty if the condition for token2 being an assignment or NULL is met.
The astTypeKindStack must be empty if the condition for token2 being an assignment or NULL is met.
Postcondition
If token2 is a valid numeric token, a new SgIntVal is pushed onto astTypeKindStack.
If token2 is NULL or an assignment, the front of astExpressionStack is moved to astTypeKindStack and removed from astExpressionStack.
Note
The function uses if blocks for debugging and relies on SgProject::get_verbose() to control logging output.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate internal state.

This function iterates through the specified number of labels currently stored in the astLabelSymbolStack. For each label, it creates a new SgLabelRefExp pointing to the symbol at the front of the stack, prepends it to a new SgExprListExp, and then removes that symbol from the stack. The resulting list of expressions is then pushed onto the astExpressionStack. This implementation is used to build the label list for computed goto statements.

Parameters
countThe number of labels to extract from the astLabelSymbolStack and include in the generated expression list.
Precondition
The astLabelSymbolStack must contain at least count elements to avoid undefined behavior during the pop operations.
Postcondition
The first count elements are removed from astLabelSymbolStack.
A new SgExprListExp containing count SgLabelRefExp elements is pushed onto the astExpressionStack.
Note
If SgProject::get_verbose() is greater than DEBUG_RULE_COMMENT_LEVEL, the function will print a debug message to stdout.

This function handles the semantic action for real literal constants in a C-like language. It parses the text of the real constant token and creates an SgFloatVal node. If a kind parameter is provided (e.g., to distinguish between float, double, etc.), it appends the kind text to the constant's text representation using an underscore. The resulting expression is then pushed onto the astExpressionStack.

Note that as of 02/14/2011, SgLongLongDoubleVal is not supported, so all real constants are processed as SgFloatVal.

Parameters
realConstantA pointer to the Token_t representing the actual numeric value of the real literal. Must not be NULL and must have a non-NULL text field.
kindParamA pointer to a Token_t representing the type/kind of the real constant (e.g., 'f' for float). Can be NULL if no kind is specified.
Precondition
realConstant must not be NULL.
realConstant->text must not be NULL.
Postcondition
A new SgFloatVal expression is created and pushed to the front of the astExpressionStack.
The source position of the new SgFloatVal is set to match realConstant.
Note
This implementation is wrapped in if !SKIP_C_ACTION_IMPLEMENTATION.

This function processes a signed real literal constant by checking for the presence of a sign token (e.g., "+" or "-"). If a sign token is provided, the function retrieves the top expression from the astExpressionStack, verifies it is a SgValueExp of type V_SgFloatVal, and modifies the underlying numeric value and its string representation to reflect the sign. Specifically, if the sign is "-", the numeric value is negated and the string is prefixed with "-". If the sign is "+", the string is prefixed with "+".

Parameters
signA pointer to a Token_t representing the sign of the literal. If NULL, no modification is performed.
Precondition
The astExpressionStack must not be empty.

If sign is not NULL, the expression at the front of astExpressionStack must have a variant type of V_SgFloatVal.
Postcondition
If sign is "-" and the expression is a V_SgFloatVal, the numeric value of the float is negated and the string representation is updated with a leading "-".
If sign is "+" and the expression is a V_SgFloatVal, the string representation is updated with a leading "+".
Warning
The function calls ROSE_ABORT() if the expression type is not V_SgFloatVal when a sign is present.
The function assumes that the astExpressionStack contains a valid SgValueExp at the front.
Note
This implementation relies on the astExpressionStack being correctly managed by the caller.
The function uses if 0 blocks for legacy debugging code which is currently inactive.

This function handles the construction of a variable declaration (SgVariableDeclaration) by utilizing data previously saved on the stack. It is functionally similar to the R441 component-attr-spec-list logic. The implementation involves updating the statement's numeric label, verifying the declaration type, and synchronizing the start and end construction positions of the declaration with the first and last variables in the declaration list.

Parameters
labelA pointer to a Token_t representing the label for the declaration statement.
numAttributesThe number of attributes associated with the declaration.
eosA pointer to a Token_t representing the end-of-statement token.
Precondition
The ifndef SKIP_C_ACTION_IMPLEMENTATION block requires that eos is not null.
The top of the scope stack must be either an SgBasicBlock or an SgClassDefinition.
The astNodeStack and astBaseTypeStack must be empty.
The object stored in DeclAttributes must be identifiable as an SgVariableDeclaration.
The declaration and the variables within the declaration must have valid startOfConstruct pointers.
Postcondition
The numeric label of the declaration in DeclAttributes is set to the provided label.
The startOfConstruct and endOfConstruct of the declaration are updated to match the startOfConstruct of the first and last variables in the declaration list, respectively.
The DeclAttributes pointer is reset.
Warning
If the declaration in DeclAttributes is not an SgVariableDeclaration, an error is printed to stderr and the program is aborted via ROSE_ABORT().
Note
This function relies on the global state of DeclAttributes and the scope stack.
The implementation is wrapped in a conditional compilation check for if !SKIP_C_ACTION_IMPLEMENTATION.

This function manages the internal state of the type parameter and expression stacks during the processing of C-style action type parameters. It determines whether to push a new asterisk expression onto the stack or to move an existing expression from the expression stack to the type parameter stack. The function also provides verbose logging if the global debug level allows it. Note that as of a specific update (9/28/2010), this function is primarily utilized for the length parameter rather than every type parameter.

Parameters

If hasAsterisk is false, the front element of astExpressionStack is moved to the front of astTypeParameterStack.

The function uses if 0 blocks for legacy debugging code that is currently disabled.
The function relies on the global SgProject::get_verbose() level to determine if logging is performed.
